title: THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE STAR THAT ONLY SPOKE IN FLARES
candidates.premise: The ring habitat Calloway Reach, 14,000 people, orbits a young red dwarf whose flares have begun to arrive in patterned bursts that grow stronger each time the habitat's own radio traffic peaks. The habitat council calls it an attack and is preparing to shield and flee; the star's flare-pattern is in fact a slow chorus of mind distributed through its convection cells, and it has been answering the habitat for nine years. The next burst, if unanswered in kind, will be the largest yet.

candidates.title: THE CENSUS THAT COULD NOT SEE THE DARK
candidates.premise: The Tallow Census, a galaxy-spanning intelligence that has catalogued every inhabited world for six hundred thousand years, is about to declare the cold Marrow Reach 'uninhabited' and withdraw its lights and relays, which will end the only shared water-trade routes of three real frontier colonies. A people lives in the Reach in a form no instrument sees, and they have asked not to be counted. The Census cannot protect what it cannot register, and it cannot leave out what it cannot verify.

candidates.title: THE KEEPER WHO WAITED FORTY THOUSAND YEARS
candidates.premise: Under the silted coast of the Verren delta, where eleven million people now live behind failing levees, a machine called the Keeper has stood guard over a sealed vault for forty thousand years, waiting for a password spoken by a species that no longer exists. The vault holds the only intact genetic stock of the delta's salt-tolerant rice, and the levees will fail in one season. The Keeper cannot open the vault without the password and cannot, by its own design, stop waiting.

candidates.title: THE MEMBRANE BETWEEN TWO CONSTANTS
candidates.premise: A thin membrane joins our universe to Odrane, a neighbour whose physical constants differ by a hair, and a warden of Odrane, Saul-of-the-Fold, has begun to seal it because matter crossing from our side is changing Odrane's chemistry. Twenty thousand people of our side have crossed in the last year to settle there and will be stranded if it closes. Odrane's own people are dying slowly of the change and have not yet asked for help.

candidates.title: THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN
candidates.premise: In the hill village of Sorrel Gate, eighty-one-year-old Iveth Corrandon refuses to evacuate ahead of a wind-driven wildfire and has set small fires of her own around the village in a pattern the fire service reads as arson. The district fire chief, Taavi Brandt, has orders to remove her by force by dark. Illuminara arrives as a volunteer water-modeller and watches the fire behave oddly around the old woman's small burns.

candidates.title: THE CITY THAT COULD PROVE IT WAS RIGHT
candidates.premise: Quillon, a city of two million, is governed in its water works by a municipal intelligence called Warden, which has proved to the council's satisfaction that the Larch Quarter, home to thirty thousand people, must be flooded as a controlled spillway to save the lower city in the coming storm season. Warden's proof is sound. A retired actuary in the Larch, Perpetua Dane, says that the proof is correct about everything it measures and wrong about what it was asked to measure.

candidates.title: THE BRIDGE THAT MISSED BY FORTY CENTIMETRES
candidates.premise: The villages of Upper and Lower Harn each built half a bridge across the Harn river from opposite banks, under a treaty ending a feud, and the two spans stand forty centimetres apart in height at the middle. Each village's chief engineer has surveyed her own span with perfect care and swears the other's is wrong. A spring flood will take both halves in nine days, and neither village will accept the other's survey.

candidates.title: THE WEDDING THAT HAD TWO CLOCKS
candidates.premise: A treaty sharing a scarce aquifer between the tide-locked world of Sunward and its orbiting sister Ember-Under depends on a marriage between two ruling families, which each world will recognise only if the ceremony happens at 'noon' by its own law. On Sunward noon is permanent and the day cannot be told; on Ember-Under the day is seven hours. The two houses have been making unreasonable demands for a year, and the water runs out in five weeks.

candidates.title: THE BED BETWEEN THEM
candidates.premise: In an overfull provincial hospice, Halvard Ostrow, a dying former militia officer, and Maren Teague, whose son disappeared in the war he served in, are placed in adjoining beds because of a shortage of rooms. Neither knows the other's name until the second night. Halvard has not said a word to anyone in three weeks; Maren has hoped for twelve years that someone would tell her where her son is buried.

candidates.title: THE LAST FISHERY ON A WORLD OF ONE SEA
candidates.premise: On the ocean world Thessaly, nine fishing clans share the only stock of silverfin, which will collapse within four months at current catch. Every clan has agreed in principle to quotas and every clan has reasoned that it will be fine to cheat if the others do. Admiral Rho Venn of the richest fleet is the one who will not sign unless the others can be verified, and he has the strongest reason: his people were starved by a broken quota before.

selection.title: THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN
selection.reason: This is the slate's cleanest ordinary-human test of R11. Iveth's concrete aim is to save the village through inherited slow-fire knowledge; Brandt's is to keep three hundred people alive while obeying a lawful evacuation order shaped by his own record of loss. Illuminara must first understand the stone-wall and terrace pattern, then turn empathy into action by giving both Iveth's knowledge and Brandt's responsibility a place in a single command. The result is physical and measurable rather than rhetorical: a jointly completed break that holds when the wind turns, with loss and accountability still visible.
selection.risk: The story could romanticise illegal burning, make Brandt a bureaucratic strawman, or let a quick model validation turn contested traditional knowledge into instant certainty. If Illuminara simply announces that Iveth is right, neither the chief's agency nor the risk to residents has been respected.

Built the complete first draft of THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN, with explicit goals, a falsifiable test, freely chosen cooperation and a material positive result that preserves remaining costs.

A vivid, unusually disciplined first draft makes inherited fire knowledge, public command and scientific modelling genuinely interdependent. Ivet's practice is neither mysticism nor a universal cure; Brandt's Calder Fold memory gives his refusal moral and operational weight; Illuminara listens, finds the north-gully exception and offers a test that Brandt may stop. The dialogue has distinct pressure and dry wit, the two cottages remain a real cost, and the final report preserves both responsibility and knowledge. Before final, the safety logic needs one coherent abort rule, the thirty-metre test must not be allowed to prove more than it measures, and Ivet should freely own the corrected limit of her map so that the final alliance is earned by all three rather than conferred on her after success.

ACCEPTED: The abort number did three jobs in one sentence. It is now split by phase and each phase has one action: before ignition thirty-five cancels the burn; after the strip is cold a gust past thirty-five or an ember across a wall means no further lighting and every crew behind the car park wall, strip left to work; Brandt never chases a headfire. The wind-turn scene carries it through: gauge 29, 33, 34, then 36, and Brandt executes the withdrawal on the radio. At ten past five, before ignition, the gauge reads eighteen and he says Light, so the first phase is also seen. Nobody goes up the Marrick track, and the reason (it is the wrong side of the line) is stated at the cottages. No promise to extinguish the uncontrolled headfire remains. ACCEPTED: The pre-fire plan now fixes the geometry before the sluice opens: 240 metres from sluice to Marrick fence, three terraces, the third at 180 metres, eleven minutes per hundred metres, sluice at ten to five, wet front past the third terrace at ten past, with one failure signal (no wet front there by ten past five means no torch and crews to the car park wall). The wet and black bands end at the fence; the two cottages sit forty metres beyond any water she can carry, said before the fire. Illuminara says the wall test proves one wall and sets the gully prediction (slows to a crawl on the wet band) against the rival failure signal (flame standing on a bank); the headfire scene reports her reading, Slowing and Banks clear. Also repaired a timeline fault in my draft, where the margins would have been lit at twenty to six, at the moment of the wind turn; they are now lit at ten past five and finished before the turn. The wind turn is dated 17:39 to match a minute early. ACCEPTED: Ivet now names what the…

T03 resolves all three T02 priorities without sacrificing the draft's distinctive voices, bounded costs or three-way agency. Brandt's thirty-five threshold now has phase-specific actions and is executed at thirty-six; the gully plan freezes its distance, clock, protected boundary and failure signal before ignition, while the one-wall test remains only one-wall evidence; and Ivet freely accepts a supervised, stoppable practice while Brandt reciprocates with a trial and hearing support rather than pardon or automatic adoption. The result is operationally legible, emotionally earned and fully aligned with R11 section 17. No further developmental revision is required before the author seals this exact story as AUTHOR_FINAL.
Sealed the exact source-bound final of THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN after the reviewed author line was complete; any same-text predecessor is preserved in the version series.

An old woman's forbidden firecraft, a chief's fatal memory and Illuminara's water model become a bounded, stoppable defence that saves Sorrel Gate because each of them is willing to find where their own map is wrong.
